title: Use a decimal value
summary: Fortran: Use a decimal value. Try 3.5. Try a small example and check what happens.
introduction: real holds a decimal value. The F3.1 format prints one digit after the decimal point.
learningObjectives: Use a decimal value with Fortran

blocks.text: Install GNU Fortran. Save each example as lesson.f90, run gfortran -std=f2008 lesson.f90 -o lesson, then run it.

blocks.title: Use a decimal value
blocks.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
real :: length = 2.5
write(*,'(F3.1)') length
end program lesson

blocks.text: The real value is 2.5. F3.1 reserves three places with one decimal place.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Choose a wider output format for a wider number.
